candidates.name: Acute Coronary Syndrome
support_spans: 1 hour of acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to his left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea
Initial serum troponin I level: 1.159 ng/mL (normal range ≤0.028 ng/mL)
95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with acute coronary syndrome.

candidates.name: ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
support_spans: 2-mm ST-segment elevation in avR
Reciprocal ST-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF
contradict_spans: Upsloping ST-segment depression leads V1 through V6
candidates.why: The patient's ECG findings are partially consistent with STEMI, but the upsloping ST-segment depression in multiple leads is atypical.

candidates.why: The patient's ECG findings and elevated troponin level are consistent with NSTEMI.

candidates.name: Variant Angina (Prinzmetal's Angina)
support_spans: acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to his left arm, accompanied by sweating and nausea
Six hours prior, he had experienced similar chest pain at rest that resolved spontaneously after 30 minutes
contradict_spans: Initial serum troponin I level: 1.159 ng/mL (normal range ≤0.028 ng/mL)
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms of acute, severe chest pain at rest and spontaneous resolution are consistent with variant angina, but the elevated troponin level suggests myocardial infarction.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be easily missed due to its rarity and similarity in presentation to other causes of chest pain.

candidates.name: Myocardial Infarction with Normal Coronary Arteries (MINCA)
support_spans: Initial serum troponin I level: 1.159 ng/mL (normal range ≤0.028 ng/mL)
95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery
candidates.why: The patient's elevated troponin level and coronary artery stenosis are consistent with myocardial infarction, but the presence of normal left ventricular ejection fraction and hypomotility in the anterior wall may suggest MINCA.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be underdiagnosed due to its rarity and the need for coronary angiography to rule out significant coronary artery disease.

candidates.name: Hypertensive Emergency with Cardiac Involvement
support_spans: blood pressure 170/109 mm Hg
Initial serum troponin I level: 1.159 ng/mL (normal range ≤0.028 ng/mL)
contradict_spans: Jugular venous pressure was not elevated, lungs were clear
candidates.why: The patient's severely elevated blood pressure and elevated troponin level are consistent with hypertensive emergency with cardiac involvement.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be easily missed due to its rarity and the need for careful consideration of the patient's blood pressure and cardiac markers.
